name: Question 12
problem:
Several egg cartons were checked for cracked eggs. The number of cracked eggs in each carton was recorded below. If $N$ is the number of cracked eggs in a carton, what is the expected value of $N?$

| Number of Cartons | $10$ | $7$ | $2$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cracked Eggs | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

We're given the frequencies of the cracked eggs, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of cartons is $10+7+2+1=20,$ so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(N=0)=f(0) & =\frac{10}{20}=\frac{1}{2} \\ P(N=1)=f(1) & =\frac{7}{20} \\ P(N=2)=f(2) & =\frac{2}{20}=\frac{1}{10} \\ P(N=3)=f(3) & =\frac{1}{20}\end{aligned}
$$

We organize these results in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{7}{20}$ | $\frac{1}{10}$ | $\frac{1}{20}$ |

Now, summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[N] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{2})+1(\frac{7}{20})+2(\frac{1}{10})+3(\frac{1}{20}) \\  & =0+\frac{7}{20}+\frac{2}{10}+\frac{3}{20} \\  & =\frac{7}{20}+\frac{4}{20}+\frac{3}{20} \\  & =\frac{7+4+3}{20} \\  & =\frac{14}{20} \\  & =\frac{7}{10} \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$

Several egg cartons were checked for cracked eggs. The number of cracked eggs in each carton was recorded below. If N is the number of cracked eggs in a carton, what is the expected value of N?

Number of Cartons 10 7 2 1
Cracked Eggs 0 1 2 3
a
0.7
b
 1
c
 1.4
d
 0.4
e
 2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The expected value of a discrete random variable X with probability mass function f(x) defined over a set S is given by

E[X]=∑x∈Sx⋅f(x).

We're given the frequencies of the cracked eggs, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of cartons is 10+7+2+1=20, so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

P(N=0)=f(0)=1020=12P(N=1)=f(1)=720P(N=2)=f(2)=220=110P(N=3)=f(3)=120

We organize these results in the table below.

x 0 1 2 3
f(x) 12 720 110 120

Now, summing up the products of each value of X and its associated probability, we get

E[N]=0⋅f(0)+1⋅f(1)+2⋅f(2)+3⋅f(3)=0(12)+1(720)+2(110)+3(120)=0+720+210+320=720+420+320=7+4+320=1420=710=0.7.
